units.title: Introduction to DBMS
topics: Data Models: ER Model, Relational Model

keyDefinitions.DBMS: A software system that manages and organizes data in a database, providing mechanisms for storing, retrieving, updating, and managing data.
keyDefinitions.Entity: A real-world object or concept that has an independent existence in the database.
keyDefinitions.Attribute: A property or characteristic of an entity.
keyDefinitions.Primary Key: A minimal set of attributes that uniquely identifies each tuple in a relation.
keyDefinitions.Foreign Key: An attribute that references the primary key of another relation, establishing a link between two tables.

units.title: Relational Model & SQL
topics: Relational Algebra: Select, Project, Join, Union, Difference
SQL DML: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, SELECT
Joins: INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL OUTER

keyDefinitions.Relational Algebra: A procedural query language that provides a set of operations to work on relations.
keyDefinitions.View: A virtual table defined by a SELECT query, providing data abstraction.
keyDefinitions.Index: A data structure that improves the speed of data retrieval operations on a database table.

keyDefinitions.Normalization: The process of organizing data to reduce redundancy and improve data integrity.
keyDefinitions.1NF: A relation is in 1NF if all attributes contain only atomic (indivisible) values.
keyDefinitions.2NF: A relation is in 2NF if it is in 1NF and every non-key attribute is fully functionally dependent on the primary key.
keyDefinitions.3NF: A relation is in 3NF if it is in 2NF and there are no transitive dependencies.
keyDefinitions.BCNF: A stronger version of 3NF where for every functional dependency X→Y, X must be a superkey.

units.title: Transactions & Concurrency
topics: Concurrency Problems: Lost Update, Dirty Read, Unrepeatable Read

keyDefinitions.ACID: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability – properties that guarantee database transactions are processed reliably.
keyDefinitions.Deadlock: A situation where two or more transactions wait for each other to release locks, causing all to be stuck indefinitely.
keyDefinitions.2PL: Two-Phase Locking – a concurrency control method where transactions acquire all locks before releasing any.

units.title: Storage & Indexing
topics: Indexing: Dense vs Sparse, Primary vs Secondary

units.title: Introduction & Process Management
topics: Process Scheduling: FCFS, SJF, Round Robin, Priority

keyDefinitions.Process: A program in execution, including the program code, stack, data section, and OS resources.
keyDefinitions.PCB: Process Control Block – a data structure maintained by the OS for each process containing process state, registers, memory limits, etc.
keyDefinitions.Context Switch: The process of saving the state of a currently running process and loading the state of the next scheduled process.

units.title: Process Synchronization
topics: Classic Problems: Dining Philosophers, Producer-Consumer, Readers-Writers

units.title: Memory Management
topics: Page Replacement Algorithms: FIFO, LRU, Optimal

keyDefinitions.Virtual Memory: A technique that allows execution of processes that may not be completely in memory, creating an illusion of a large address space.
keyDefinitions.TLB: Translation Lookaside Buffer – a hardware cache that speeds up virtual-to-physical address translation.
keyDefinitions.Thrashing: A condition where excessive paging activity causes the OS to spend more time swapping pages than executing processes.

units.title: File Systems
topics: File Allocation Methods: Contiguous, Linked, Indexed
Disk Scheduling: FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN

units.title: Transport & Application Layer
topics: TCP: Connection, Flow Control, Congestion Control

units.title: Software Design
topics: Design Principles: Abstraction, Modularity, Cohesion, Coupling
UML Diagrams: Class, Sequence, Use Case, Activity

units.title: Software Testing
topics: Testing Levels: Unit, Integration, System, Acceptance
Black Box and White Box Testing
Test Case Design: Boundary Value, Equivalence Partitioning

keyDefinitions.DFA: Deterministic Finite Automaton – a finite state machine where each state has exactly one transition for each input symbol.
keyDefinitions.NFA: Nondeterministic Finite Automaton – a finite state machine where each state can have zero or multiple transitions for an input symbol.
keyDefinitions.Regular Language: A language that can be recognized by a finite automaton or expressed as a regular expression.
